subject: Wardrobes for sloped ceilings and alcoves
hook: Loft room or chimney alcove? Avoid these five wardrobe mistakes.
ig:
Loft room or chimney alcove? Avoid these five wardrobe mistakes.

Fitted wardrobes for sloped ceilings and alcoves are where made-to-measure furniture earns its keep. They are also where the classic mistakes happen:

1. Leaving the low end of a slope empty. It is ideal for drawers.
2. Putting long hanging under the short side. Tall items go where the ceiling is tallest.
3. Choosing doors that hit the ceiling as they swing.
4. Assuming a chimney alcove is deep enough for side-on hanging. Measure first.
5. Forgetting that old walls are rarely straight. Scribed fillers make it look built in.

Get these right and an awkward room ends up with more usable storage than a square one.

Save this before you start planning, and see our fitted wardrobes via the link in bio.
fb:
Loft conversions and older houses with chimney breasts make for lovely bedrooms and very awkward wardrobes.

The five things we see most: the low end of a slope left empty, long dresses squeezed under the short side, doors that catch the ceiling, alcoves that turn out too shallow for hangers, and wonky walls that leave gaps.

All five are easy to avoid at the design stage. Swipe through for how.
